 Tech The90 Gem pendant tracks how much UVA and UVB light actually reaches your skin
 By t2ONLINE Web Desk 
 Published: 8 Nov 2026, 12:07PM | 2 min read Picture: The90
 Advertisement The90, a preventative skin health company based in Walnut Creek, California, has a wearable that measures how much ultraviolet light reaches the wearer, rather than relying on a broad, location-based UV index.
 The device, called The90 Gem, is a pendant necklace holding a circular sensor in a titanium case, in silver or gold finishes. It tracks exposure to UVA rays, which are associated with long-term skin ageing, and UVB rays, which are more closely tied to sunburn.
 The company takes its name from the figure that up to 90 per cent of visible skin ageing and premature skin damage is linked to cumulative, everyday UV exposure.
 The Gem pairs with a companion app on Android and iOS. Users start with a questionnaire on their skin type, then log daily sunscreen use and sun-protective habits to build a personal skin profile.
 The app combines that profile with live sensor readings to give real-time guidance: personalised UV thresholds, reminders to reapply sunscreen, advice on when to cover up and suggested windows for time in the sun. It can also show whether a shaded spot is offering meaningful protection. It includes vitamin D targets, clothing recommendations for the conditions and steps to take after time outdoors.
 Because the sensor is worn on the body, it records the UV that reaches the user through the day, whether through a window, in a car, in the shade or on a beach. UVA rays can pass through glass.
 The battery lasts around a week on a single charge, and the sensor and case are splash-proof. The Gem is currently designed for women. Versions for men and children are planned, along with other ways of wearing the sensor.
 The90 was founded by chief executive Stacy Salvi, who spent more than a decade in the wearables industry. The daughter of a dermatologist, she most recently helped build a smart ring for women.
 “True innovation happens when deep technology is wrapped in a high-end, modular aesthetic that women actually want to wear,” said Salvi. “We are on the cusp of a skincare revolution. The90 transforms sunscreen from a one-time morning ritual into an adaptive, responsive system built around your actual UV load. We want to empower women to stop guessing and finally own their light, strategically harnessing the sun for optimal health.”
 The company’s backers include Chase Fisher, founder of Blenders Eyewear; Alex Haro, founder of Life360 and Hubble; Steven Borelli, founder of Cuts Clothing; SpaceStation Investments; and Lauryn Bosstick, podcast host and founder of The Skinny Confidential, who is also joining The90 as an adviser.
 “Women are already investing in SPF, treatments, tools, and routines to protect their skin, but when it comes to sun exposure, most of us are still guessing,” said Bosstick. “The UV index on your phone doesn’t know your skin, your sunscreen, or the small moments of exposure that happen throughout the day. The90 gives women the missing data to make smarter decisions and stay ahead of skin aging before it starts.”
